paper.title: Introducing the Illustris Project: Simulating the coevolution of dark and visible matter in the Universe
paper.authors: Mark Vogelsberger, Shy Genel, Volker Springel et al.

thesis: Our model predicts a halo mass dependent impact of baryonic effects on the halo mass function and the masses of haloes caused by feedback from supernova and active galactic nuclei.

reconstruction.scope: abstract-level graph with retained full text

nodes.title: Research question
nodes.body: What does the reported model reveal when the target system is simulated?

nodes.title: Choose model and boundary conditions
nodes.body: We introduce the Illustris Project, a series of large-scale hydrodynamical simulations of galaxy formation.

nodes.title: Run the numerical experiment
nodes.body: The highest resolution simulation, Illustris-1, covers a volume of $(106.5\,{\rm Mpc})^3$, has a dark mass resolution of ${6.26 \times 10^{6}\,{\rm M}_\odot}$, and an initial baryonic matter mass resolution of ${1.26 \times 10^{6}\,{\rm M}_\odot}$.

nodes.title: Primary reported result
nodes.body: In the well-resolved regime the simulation reproduces the observed mix of early-type and late-type galaxies.

nodes.title: Published conclusion
nodes.body: Our model predicts a halo mass dependent impact of baryonic effects on the halo mass function and the masses of haloes caused by feedback from supernova and active galactic nuclei.
